title: Idempotent source-Environment recreate at destination
description: The system shall recreate every source GitHub Actions Environment at the destination with wait_timer, prevent_self_review, reviewers, and deployment_branch_policy from the analyze-time snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: PUT /repos/.../environments/{name} with snapshot config | Branch policies POSTed individually | Idempotent: re-running does not duplicate policies | Runs BEFORE secret-stub creation so env-scoped stubs land on existing envs
notes: Requires destination reviewers (users/teams) to exist; falls back per AMP-F-PMG-120

title: Reviewer-strip fallback on Environment 422
description: On 422 from the destination environment PUT, the system shall retry without the reviewers field and flag the env in the consolidated post-migration comment so operators can re-assign reviewers manually.
acceptance_criteria: 422 typically means reviewer principal does not exist at destination | Retry without reviewers preserves other env config | Flagged env listed under Environments section of consolidated comment | Operator re-triggers via cmd:upsert-envs once reviewers exist
notes: Most common cause: SCIM-provisioned reviewers not yet present

title: Retry destination clone on transient post-migration state
description: The verification step shall retry the destination git clone with bounded exponential backoff when it fails with a transient post-migration state (HTTP 403 / repository disabled), and fail fast on non-transient errors.
acceptance_criteria: Transient stderr signatures (is disabled / read-only / 403) trigger retry | Bounded attempts with exponential backoff | Non-transient errors (404/auth) return after the first attempt | A clone that succeeds on retry verifies normally
notes: gh gei briefly leaves a freshly-migrated repo disabled before GitHub releases it

title: Auto-create environment for env-scoped secret/variable stubs
description: Before writing an env-scoped secret/variable stub, the system shall idempotently create the named destination environment so the stub PUT does not 404 when the environment was never a real source Actions Environment.
acceptance_criteria: Distinct env names collected from env-scoped secret and variable refs | PUT /repos/.../environments/{env} issued once per env before its stubs | Idempotent — an env already created by environments-recreate is left unchanged | Env-create failure is swallowed and the per-stub failure is recorded
notes: A workflow can reference an environment name that was never configured as a real Environment object

title: Unarchive destination for post-migration write steps
description: When the migrated destination repo is archived (gh gei preserves the source archived flag), the system shall temporarily unarchive it for the duration of the post-migration write steps and restore the archived state afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: Archived destination unarchived before branch protection / custom properties / stubs / migration-fixes | Archived state restored in a finally block even when a wrapped step raises | No-op when the destination is not archived | Applied by /migrate and every /upsert-* handler
notes: Branch protection and other writes otherwise 403 with repository was archived so is read-only

title: Stamp secrets-recreate and environments outcome labels
description: The system shall stamp one secrets-recreate:* label and one environments:* label per migration with outcome (none, created, partial, failed, skipped, rate-limit-deferred).
acceptance_criteria: POST_MIGRATE_STAGES enforces mutual exclusivity within each family | rate-limit-deferred set when API budget too low to safely create | Re-trigger via cmd:upsert-secrets / cmd:upsert-envs clears and re-stamps
notes: Outcomes surface in consolidated post-migration comment via migration_verify

title: Idempotent classic branch protection recreate at destination
description: On /dryrun and /migrate the system shall attempt to recreate each source-side classic branch protection rule at the matching destination branch using PUT /repos/{org}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection with the structured config captured at analyze time. If the marker is absent (issue analyzed before the feature shipped) the system shall re-fetch the rules from source. Failures shall never roll back the migration.
acceptance_criteria: Reads <!-- amp:branch-protection-data --> marker via amp.issue_parser.parse_branch_protection_data | Falls back to GitHubAnalyzer.get_branch_protection_rules against source when marker absent | Per-branch GET /branches/{name} to distinguish skipped (404) from failed (403) | PUT with strict/contexts normalized | 422 on restriction actors strips restrictions and retries | Outcome folded into consolidated verification comment as 'Branch protection' check | Runs on both /migrate and /dryrun | All exceptions caught — migration outcome unaffected
notes: Cross-tenant push restriction actors typically do not resolve at the destination — strip-and-retry preserves the rest of the rule. Rulesets are out of scope.

title: Stamp branch-protection dest outcome label
description: The system shall stamp exactly one branch-protection:dest-* label per migration: dest-applied (all rules landed), dest-partial (some applied, others skipped/failed), dest-failed (no rules applied), or dest-skipped (no matching branches at destination).
acceptance_criteria: Labels added to PRESERVE_PREFIXES_DEFAULT so re-analysis preserves them | POST_MIGRATE_STAGES stage 'branch-protection-dest' enforces mutual exclusivity | Label stamped from BranchProtectionOutcome.label() after recreate completes
notes: Surfaces in operator's consolidated post-migration comment and in the destination handoff issue

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-secrets
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-secrets and cmd:upsert-secrets (formerly /create-secret-stubs) to manually re-run idempotent secret/variable stub creation after destination environments are added or transient failures clear.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-secrets handler re-reads issue marker | Delegates to same helper as auto-run | cmd:upsert-secrets dispatched to /upsert-secrets | Idempotent — safe to spam | Stamps upserted:secrets on success
notes: Most useful after operator manually adds env that 422'd

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-envs
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-envs and cmd:upsert-envs (formerly /recreate-environments) to manually re-run idempotent Environment recreate at the destination after reviewers are provisioned or transient failures clear.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-envs handler re-reads issue marker | Delegates to same helper as auto-run | cmd:upsert-envs dispatched to /upsert-envs | Idempotent — safe to spam | Stamps upserted:envs on success
notes: Most useful after SCIM provisions reviewers post-migration

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-protection
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-protection and cmd:upsert-protection to manually re-run idempotent classic branch protection rule recreation at the destination after transient failures clear.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-protection reads analyze-time marker (or backfills from source for GH-source) | Idempotent — safe to spam | Stamps upserted:protection on success | GitHub source only
notes: Classic branch protection is a GitHub-source-only concept

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-properties
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-properties and cmd:upsert-properties to manually re-run idempotent custom-properties carry-through to the destination after schema is created or transient failures clear.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-properties reads custom properties from issue body | On 422 creates schema at dest org level then retries | Stamps upserted:properties on success
notes: GitHub source only — only GitHub captures custom properties at analyze time

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-fixes
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-fixes and cmd:upsert-fixes to manually re-push the amp/migration-fixes branch (submodule URL / workflow uses: / CODEOWNERS rewrites) after sibling repos migrate.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-fixes recomputes rewrites against current destination tree | Force-updates the branch if it already exists | Stamps upserted:submodules / upserted:workflows / upserted:codeowners for whichever rewrites applied | Idempotent
notes: Most useful after sibling repos migrate so cross-repo references can resolve

title: Manual re-trigger upsert-validate
description: The platform shall expose /upsert-validate and cmd:upsert-validate to manually re-run the post-migration branch/tag/commit count validation against the destination.
acceptance_criteria: /upsert-validate compares analyze-time source counts (from issue body) against live destination | Excludes amp/migration-fixes branch | Skips SHA assertion when lfs:oversized | Stamps upserted:validate on pass
notes: Useful to recheck after a remediation push

title: Pre-flight PAT validation before claim
description: The platform shall whoami-probe the resolved source and destination tokens before /migrate, /dryrun, and /remigrate claim the issue, flip status:*-running, post the claim marker, clone the source baseline, delete the sandbox/target, or invoke gh gei; a 401/403 returns a blocker comment naming the exact env var to refresh; network errors and non-auth 4xx are inconclusive (warn-only); AMP_SKIP_TOKEN_PREFLIGHT=true bypasses for incident scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Source github probe reuses amp/auth_status.py _probe_github_token | Dest probe calls get_dest_github_client and get_organization (works for App + PAT) | Per-provider probes for ado / gitlab / bitbucket-server / bitbucket-cloud | Bitbucket Cloud blocker if BITBUCKET_EMAIL missing | 5 s timeout no retry | Blocker text names env var to refresh and includes probed URL
notes: Fixes the failure mode where an expired GH_PAT only surfaced from inside gh gei after the issue had already been claimed and status flipped

title: Short-form upserted:* done labels
description: The system shall stamp short-form upserted:* labels on each post-migrate step success (teams, secrets, envs, protection, properties, validate, submodules, workflows, codeowners) so operators can scan an issue and see at a glance which steps actually completed.
acceptance_criteria: Stamped only on success (not failure / partial / none / rate-limit-deferred) | Multi-valued: an issue can carry several at once | Surfaced as the Upserted column in CSV and Excel exports | Detailed families (migration-fixes:*
notes: etc) remain source of truth for non-success states

title: Runtime dep pynacl >=1.5
description: The secret-stub creation flow shall depend on PyNaCl >=1.5 for libsodium sealed-box encryption against destination public keys.
acceptance_criteria: pynacl>=1.5 listed in setup.py install_requires | Same constraint in requirements.txt | Used by amp/secrets_recreate.py encryption helper
notes: Required for sealed-box encryption per GitHub Actions secrets API

title: Recent committers extraction with email dedup
description: The analyzer shall extract recent committers per repo deduplicated by email so the same person under multiple display names appears once, surfacing the dedup list on the AMP issue body.
acceptance_criteria: Recent committers list ordered by most-recent first | Dedup keyed on lowercased email | Display name from first occurrence retained | List length capped to keep issue body bounded
notes: Used for destination team assignment planning

title: Opt-in hardcoded-URL scan
description: The analyzer shall optionally git-grep every tracked file for the source SCM hostname when --scan-hardcoded-urls is passed, emitting hardcoded-urls:present when matches are found.
acceptance_criteria: Off by default (adds 1–30 s per repo) | Source SCM hostname derived from provider config | Match list reported as collapsible section on issue body | hardcoded-urls:present label applied when any match
notes: Catches scripts / IaC / docs referencing source host

title: LFS object verification + auto-push at destination
description: After successful migration, the system shall enumerate source LFS pointers across all refs and probe the destination LFS Batch API for each OID, pushing any missing objects from source LFS to destination LFS and re-probing.
acceptance_criteria: Runs for any LFS-involved repo (lfs:active/historical/broken/oversized/orphan-pointers/inconsistent) not just lfs:active | git lfs ls-files --json --all enumerates source OIDs | Destination Batch API probe classifies present vs missing | Missing objects fetched then pushed via git lfs push | Re-probe after push verifies closure of gap
notes: Catches silent GEI LFS gaps on cross-tenant

title: Post-migration LFS structure re-verification
description: After migration, the system shall re-run the deep LFS scan on source and destination clones and fail validation when .gitattributes files, LFS pointers, or raw blobs did not transfer faithfully.
acceptance_criteria: .gitattributes parity (root + nested) checked | A raw blob larger than the source's largest fails (pointer smudged to raw) | Orphan pointers new at destination fail; pre-existing ones carried faithfully pass-with-note | A failed LFS check flips status:validate-failed
notes: Proves the migration carried LFS structure not just objects

title: Migration-fixes .gitattributes LFS remediation
description: The migration-fixes branch shall forward-fix the destination .gitattributes — correcting malformed LFS globs and adding filter=lfs rules for orphan-pointer paths — driven by the analyze-time amp-lfs-fixes marker on the issue body.
acceptance_criteria: Brace-expansion patterns ({*.tgz}) corrected to literal globs | filter=lfs rules appended to root .gitattributes for orphan-pointer paths | Already-covered paths skipped | Forward-fix only — history is not rewritten
notes: Operator runs git lfs migrate import to also convert existing history

title: Standalone amp audit-lfs command
description: The system shall expose amp audit-lfs to run the deep LFS audit against any repo URL without creating an issue.
acceptance_criteria: Clones the repo no-checkout with LFS smudge skipped | Runs analyze_lfs and prints markdown or --json | Exits non-zero on a hard blocker (lfs:source-missing / lfs:broken)
notes: Usable for CI / pre-migration vetting

title: CODEOWNERS rewriter on migration-fixes branch
description: The system shall rewrite @org/team mentions in CODEOWNERS files to destination owner/team via the cross-repo resolver and commit the result to the amp/migration-fixes branch.
acceptance_criteria: Scans CODEOWNERS at every path level | Provider-aware lookup via IssueIndex resolver | Unmapped teams left untouched with a // skipped comment | Sandbox mode resolves to sandbox-prefixed team names
notes: Parallel to AMP-F-PMG-020 for workflow uses: refs

title: Destination-repo handoff issue with operator-stripped checklist
description: After /dryrun and /migrate, the system shall open or update an issue on the destination repo with a verification summary, mirrored analysis sections, and a 'What you need to do' checklist scoped for the repo owner (no operator-only content).
acceptance_criteria: Title: 'AMP dry-run preview — YYYY-MM-DD' / 'AMP migration report — YYYY-MM-DD' | Operator-only sections (routing labels
notes: amp-id marker) stripped | Collapsible per-section detail in <details> blocks | Wiped on subsequent /dryrun; preserved on /migrate
column19: Durable handoff for repo owners with no AMP control-plane access

title: Migration-fixes pull-request call-out in destination handoff issue
description: When AMP opened a pull request for the amp/migration-fixes branch, the destination handoff issue shall link that PR in the 'What was auto-fixed' summary and in each auto-corrected section banner, stating it is awaiting review and can be merged once it looks right.
acceptance_criteria: 'What was auto-fixed' summary links the PR and flags it as awaiting review when `pr_url` is set | ✅ auto-fixed and 🟨 partial section banners link the same PR | Falls back to the branch link / branch-merge wording when `pr_url` is empty (PR creation failed)
notes: Surfaces the existing best-effort PR (AMP-F-PMG-005) so repo owners review and merge rather than merging a bare branch by hand

title: LFS push gap repair with classified outcome
description: On lfs:dest-missing the repair handler shall probe source vs destination LFS servers, classify the gap as source-missing / dest-auth / dest-saml / dest-quota, optionally retry the push serially with debug, and stamp the classified label so operators know exactly what to fix.
acceptance_criteria: Source LFS Batch API probe to confirm OID existence | Destination Batch API upload-accept probe (no bytes sent) | Serial retry uses lfs.concurrenttransfers=1 lfs.batch=false with AMP_LFS_DEBUG=1 | One of lfs:source-missing / lfs:dest-auth / lfs:dest-saml / lfs:dest-quota applied | Diagnostic detail posted to issue
notes: Most-common silent failure on cross-tenant GHEC-DR migrations

title: LFS push diagnostics surfaced in advisor comment
description: The advisor comment shall surface LFS push diagnostics — per-OID error counts, server endpoints probed, classification outcome — as a collapsible section so operators have full context without inspecting workflow logs.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic block rendered as collapsible <details> | Includes endpoints probed and per-OID HTTP status summary | Sensitive tokens redacted | Only rendered when LFS-related repair handler ran
notes: Eliminates need to download workflow log artifact for LFS issues

title: Blockers / Warnings / Primary Blocker classification
description: The platform shall classify labels into Blockers (hard, migration-stopping) and Warnings (soft, manual-remediation) and expose them as project fields (Blockers, Warnings text fields; Primary Blocker single-select for grouping).
acceptance_criteria: Classification list lives in amp/blockers.py — change there, not by renaming labels | Blockers text: comma-joined hard blockers | Warnings text: comma-joined soft items (secrets:present, *:rewrite-needed, etc.) | Primary Blocker: highest-severity hard blocker for group-by | Existing items pick up new classifications on next sync
notes: Drives the 'Blocked' table view created by amp install

title: Excel export readiness + post-migration columns
description: The Excel exporter shall add columns for readiness checks and post-migration outcome labels at stable trailing positions so prior column indices stay stable for downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: New columns appended at trailing positions | Prior column indices unchanged | Conditional formatting extended to new outcome columns | scripts/export-issues.py adds matching CSV prefix columns
notes: Schema-stability contract with downstream consumers

title: System shall support local execution of migrations from an operator workstation
description: The system shall execute the same migrate / dryrun / remigrate logic on a macOS, Linux, or Windows workstation as a fallback when a GitHub Actions runner cannot complete the migration (LFS disk exhaustion, 6 h timeout, queue saturation, API rate limits).
acceptance_criteria: See child requirements
notes: Level-1 capability statement

title: amp run CLI subcommand
description: The CLI shall expose `amp run --issue <N> --repo <owner/repo> --command <migrate|dryrun|remigrate>` to invoke the same internal dispatcher verb that migration-worker.yml runs.
acceptance_criteria: Short command form maps to internal run-* verb | --dry-run validates env without side effects | --force overrides *-running state check | --skip-claim leaves labels untouched for resume scenarios
notes: Wraps amp.commands.dispatch with no behavior change

title: Environment preflight checks
description: The local-run command shall run a preflight pass that verifies: required external binaries on PATH (gh + provider-specific gh extension + git + git-lfs when LFS labels present), token resolvability (provider source token + destination via existing helpers), and that the issue is not already in progress (refuses status:*-running for the command stage unless --force; every other state runs without --force).
acceptance_criteria: Missing binaries reported with actionable install hint | Missing tokens reported per-provider | Issue in *-running rejected unless --force | Issue in any other state (analyzed / no status / dryrun-* / *-failed / *-queued / *-success) runs without --force | gh extensions probed via gh extension list (not shutil.which)
notes: Reuses helpers.get_*_github_client for tokens; no duplication

title: Local-run marker + claim protocol
description: On claim, amp run shall post an <!-- amp-local-run --> marker comment carrying operator name + hostname + UTC timestamp, then flip status:*-queued (or *-failed) to status:*-running so the dispatcher sees the issue as claimed.
acceptance_criteria: Marker comment contains LOCAL_RUN_MARKER string verbatim | Status label flipped via set_status_label (same call as dispatcher) | Prior status captured for rollback
notes: Mirrors migration-dispatcher.yml claim protocol

title: Reconciler honors local-run marker
description: The migration-queue reconciler (scripts/reconcile-queue.sh) shall skip stuck *-running issues whose most recent comment carries the <!-- amp-local-run --> marker (not the aborted variant) until AMP_LOCAL_RUN_TIMEOUT_HOURS (default 24) has elapsed.
acceptance_criteria: Active marker within timeout leaves issue alone | Active marker past AMP_LOCAL_RUN_TIMEOUT_HOURS reclaimed | Aborted marker treated as release back to CI | Marker absent: existing >2 h reclaim logic applies
notes: Prevents CI from racing a long local LFS push

title: Abort and recovery
description: On Ctrl-C or unhandled exception, amp run shall post an <!-- amp-local-run-aborted --> marker and roll the status label back to *-queued so a CI worker (or another local invocation) can take over.
acceptance_criteria: Aborted marker contains LOCAL_RUN_ABORTED_MARKER string verbatim | Status rolled back to *-queued | Reason captured in comment body | Cleanup failure is best-effort and logged
notes: Prevents stranding the issue if local run dies mid-flight

title: Local-setup bootstrap scripts
description: The system shall provide scripts/setup-local.sh (macOS/Linux) and scripts/setup-local.ps1 (Windows best-effort) that probe for each required dependency and install only what is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Python 3.11+ probed | amp installed editable if not importable | gh CLI verified | gh extensions probed via gh extension list and installed only if missing | git + git-lfs verified | Env-var template printed at end
notes: Idempotent — running twice on the same machine is a no-op on the second run

title: Local submodule-tree migration
description: The local-run command shall accept --command migrate-with-submodules to migrate a parent issue and each AMP-managed submodule locally in one pass: the full planned run order is printed and confirmed before anything runs, submodule children are migrated before the parent, the run is continue-on-failure, and a per-issue summary is printed at the end.
source_reference: amp/local.py § run_with_submodules; amp/cli.py § run; amp/issue_index.py § resolve_submodule_issues
acceptance_criteria: Planned run order (parent + every child + skipped rows) printed and confirmed before the first migration | Declining the prompt migrates nothing (exit 0) | --yes skips the prompt but still prints the plan | Children migrated before the parent | A child failure does not stop the run; remaining children + parent still run | Exit code non-zero if any issue failed | Parent with zero submodules behaves like plain migrate | Submodules with no AMP issue / ambiguous / self-reference / unparseable URL reported as skipped not failed | Submodule or parent whose destination repo already exists skipped as already-migrated
test_method: always — regardless of --force (--force only overrides the status:*-running claim guard; use /remigrate to replace a destination) | When every issue is already migrated the run exits without prompting | --dry-run prints the resolved run order without claiming or dispatching | Ctrl-C rolls back the in-flight claim and stops the tree (exit 130)
notes: Unit
column18: Reuses the single-issue preflight/claim/dispatch path per issue; submodule resolution shared with the IssueOps fan-out via resolve_submodule_issues; destination-existence probe shared via destination_repo_if_exists

title: Local recursive submodule-tree migration
description: The local-run command shall accept --command migrate-submodules-deep to migrate a parent issue and its full recursive submodule tree (all descendants) locally in one pass, migrating deepest-first so each repo's submodule URLs resolve to already-live destinations; the traversal is cycle-safe; all other behaviour (plan/confirm, continue-on-failure, already-migrated skip, --dry-run, --yes, --force semantics) matches --command migrate-with-submodules.
source_reference: amp/local.py § run_with_submodules; amp/cli.py § run; amp/issue_index.py § resolve_descendant_issues
acceptance_criteria: Resolves the full descendant tree via resolve_descendant_issues | Deepest descendants migrated before the repos that depend on them; parent last | Cycles / shared submodules migrated once | Planned run order (parent + every descendant + skipped rows) printed and confirmed before the first migration | Continue-on-failure and per-issue summary identical to the one-level command | Already-migrated descendant/parent skipped regardless of --force
notes: Recursive variant of AMP-F-LCL-070; selected via SUBMODULE_DEEP_VERB

title: Flag GEI run warnings with status:has-warnings
description: On every /dryrun and /migrate success the system shall stamp or clear an additive status:has-warnings label reflecting whether the GEI run produced warnings, and surface it as a dedicated Run Warnings column in the CSV and Excel exports.
source_reference: amp/labels.py § set_warnings_flag; amp/commands/__init__.py § _handle_dryrun; amp/commands/__init__.py § _handle_migrate; scripts/export-issues.py; amp/excel/export.py
acceptance_criteria: status:has-warnings added when run.warnings is non-empty on a successful run | removed on a later clean run (re-evaluated every run) | additive flag — coexists with status:*-success and is absent from STATUS_STAGES so set_status_label never clears it | Run Warnings export column shows Yes when the flag is present
notes: Distinct from the readiness Warnings rollup in amp.blockers; intentionally not added to the project Status single-select

title: Migration warnings section in destination handoff issue
description: When the GEI run produced warnings the destination-repo handoff issue shall include a 'Migration warnings to review' section under the 'What you need to do' checklist, with plain-language explanations of each recognized warning category plus the raw warning log.
acceptance_criteria: Section rendered only when the run produced warnings | Recognized categories (UNABLE_TO_COMPARE, LINE_NOT_FOUND_IN_DIFF, review-thread fallbacks, bodiless reviews, commit comments, work-item links, unmapped users) each get a plain-language explanation and impact note | Raw warning log included in a nested collapsed block capped at 80 lines | Links to GitHub's migration troubleshooting guide | A matching checklist item is added so the section is discoverable
notes: Reassures repo owners that GEI warnings are almost always cosmetic — code/branches/tags/history unaffected

title: GitLab migration via gl-exporter
description: The system shall migrate GitLab repositories by running gl-exporter to produce a ghe-migrator archive, uploading it to fetchable storage, and importing it via the GitHub migration GraphQL API (GL_EXPORTER_ARCHIVE source type).
acceptance_criteria: export → upload → import orchestrated by migrate_gitlab_repo | createMigrationSource type GL_EXPORTER_ARCHIVE | startRepositoryMigration polled to a terminal state | wired into /migrate and /dryrun
notes: gh gei has no GitLab source — replaces the prior non-functional gei fall-through

title: gl-exporter Docker image for GitLab export
description: The operator shall make the gl-exporter Docker image available on runners performing GitLab source migrations.
acceptance_criteria: GL_EXPORTER_IMAGE points at a pullable ref or a pre-built local tag | Docker required on the runner | Default tag gl-exporter:1.7.14
notes: gl-exporter is not on a public registry — operator builds or pushes it

title: Archive storage for GitLab migration
description: The system shall upload the gl-exporter archive to GitHub-owned blob storage by default or to Azure Blob when AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING is set.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub-owned storage needs no external account | Azure backend used when the connection string is set | Returns a URL the importer can fetch
notes: Mirrors gh bbs2gh storage options

title: GL_EXPORTER_ARCHIVE org authorization
description: The destination org shall be authorized by GitHub for GL_EXPORTER_ARCHIVE migrations before GitLab migration can run.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized org fails fast with remediation | Authorization arranged via a GitHub migration engagement | Surfaced as GitLabMigrationNotAuthorized
notes: Gated feature — outside AMP's control

title: Bitbucket Cloud migration via gh-bbc-exporter
description: The system shall migrate Bitbucket Cloud repositories by running gh bbc-exporter migrate, which exports the repo to a ghe-migrator archive, uploads it to GitHub-owned storage, and imports it via the GitHub migration API — export and import in one subprocess.
acceptance_criteria: migrate subcommand + flags built by build_migrate_args | destination PAT passed to the subprocess via the GITHUB_PAT env var (never argv) | --target-repo-visibility set from BBC_TARGET_REPO_VISIBILITY (default private) | GHES targets rejected before export — only api.github.com and *.ghe.com | wired into /migrate and /dryrun
notes: gh gei has no Bitbucket Cloud source — bbc-exporter owns export and import

title: Compiled wheel distribution
description: The system shall be distributable as a Cython-compiled, platform-tagged Python wheel that bundles config defaults, so AMP source is not present in readable form in the customer environment.
acceptance_criteria: cythonize compiles all amp/ modules except cleartext shims (__main__.py, empty __init__.py, amp/__init__.py) | compiled .py dropped from the wheel | wheel tagged cpXX-cpXX-<platform> | `amp` and `python -m amp.commands` both work from the install
notes: Native .so/.pyd; defense-in-depth, not cryptographic. Free (no license, no size cap).

title: Per-platform publish to private dist repo
description: On a v* tag the publish workflow shall matrix-build wheels per platform/Python natively and upload them as assets to a release on the private distribution repo (vars.AMP_DIST_REPO); a weekly cron refreshes the assets.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix builds linux-x64 + macOS-arm64 + windows-x64 x py3.11-3.13 | wheels uploaded to v<version> release on AMP_DIST_REPO | idempotent create-or-clobber | weekly schedule refreshes expiry | source repo never publishes source
notes: Each wheel built natively per platform (no cross-compile)

title: setup-amp wheel-vs-source install branch
description: The setup-amp composite action shall install amp from the private wheel when dist-token, version, and dist-repo are all provided, and otherwise fall back to pip install -e . (editable source).
acceptance_criteria: All three inputs set -> gh release download + pip install of the wheel | any unset -> pip install -e . | gh available before download (step order) | pip selects the matching platform wheel
notes: Additive; existing source installs unaffected

title: Revocable distribution access
description: Customer access to the distribution wheel shall be controlled by a read-scoped token (AMP_DIST_TOKEN, Contents: read on the dist repo) that can be revoked at engagement end to block new installs and upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Valid token downloads the wheel | revoked/invalid token returns 401 on gh release download | already-installed copies keep running | token reads only release assets, not source
notes: Mirrors siphon-net revoke-the-read-token lifecycle

title: Config source override (AMP_CONFIG_DIR)
description: The system shall resolve labels.yml / failure_rules.yml / project_views.yml via $AMP_CONFIG_DIR, then the repo-root sibling (editable installs), then the package-bundled copy (wheel installs).
acceptance_criteria: resolve_config returns AMP_CONFIG_DIR path when the file exists there | editable install reads repo config/ | wheel install reads amp/_bundled_config/ | per-engagement tuning without rebuilding the wheel
notes: Lets a control repo tune labels without a wheel rebuild

title: Runtime build-expiry (time-bomb)
description: Each compiled wheel shall refuse to run past a baked expiry date (default 14 days), so an installed or copied binary self-destructs after the window; CI re-pulls each run and a weekly cron refreshes the published build to stay non-expired.
acceptance_criteria: enforce_expiry() called from amp.cli group callback (update exempt) and amp.commands.main() | past EXPIRY -> exit with message | no-op in source installs | guard compiled (.so) | stopping the refresh cron expires installed+copied client binaries within the window
notes: Goes beyond siphon (which has no runtime enforcement); clock-rollback is a known bypass

title: Signed internal-license expiry bypass
description: Holders of a valid Xebia-signed internal license (Ed25519) shall bypass the build expiry until the license's own exp, so consultants are not forced onto the client refresh cadence.
source_reference: amp/_guard.py (embedded public key); scripts/sign_license.py (private key, maintainer-only)
acceptance_criteria: Valid signed token in AMP_INTERNAL_LICENSE or ~/.amp/license bypasses expiry | forged or expired token does not | only the public key is embedded so clients cannot forge | private signing key never ships
notes: Rotate the keypair (new build) to invalidate issued licenses

title: Normalized fixture seed across all five source SCMs
description: test-env/seed.py creates one self-describing fixture set (empty, small, medium, many-prs, lfs/codeowners/workflows/submodules edge cases, large-file, huge-file) across GitLab, Bitbucket Server, Azure DevOps, GitHub, and Bitbucket Cloud so every provider is exercised against an identical matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Running seed.py --only all creates the same fixture names in each SCM's configured namespace; idempotent on re-run.
notes: Hosted SCM tokens sourced from ~/.ghpats; local from test-env/.env

title: Large-file fixture exercises the blob warning band
description: A ~150 MB raw-blob fixture (large-file) yields max_blob_size in the 100-375 MB band so the analyzer emits blob:warning. Skipped on GitHub (hard 100 MB per-file reject).
acceptance_criteria: dry-analyze of large-file reports ~150 MB and emits blob:warning on gitlab/bbs/ado/bbc; not created on github.
notes: Raw blob, not LFS

title: Huge-file (400 MB) fixture exercises the migration size cutoff
description: A repo containing only a ~400 MB raw blob (huge-file-400mb) exceeds BLOB_ERROR (375 MB), so the analyzer emits blob:error and a migration of it either succeeds or fails purely on size. Skipped on GitHub.
acceptance_criteria: dry-analyze of huge-file-400mb reports ~400 MB and emits blob:error; a /migrate of its issue reaches a clean success or size-related failure.
notes: Solo file; raw blob

title: Capability-gated fixture skipping
description: PLATFORM_CAPS plus per-fixture requires tags drive fixture_allowed(), which skips fixtures a platform cannot satisfy (GitHub >100 MB reject; ADO/BBC LFS off) and logs the reason.
acceptance_criteria: fixture_allowed returns (False, reason) for the >100 MB fixtures on github and lfs fixtures on ado/bbc; unit-tested.

title: Parallel fixture seeding
description: Seeding fans out across SCMs and fixtures via a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor (--jobs / AMP_SEED_JOBS); concurrent large pushes to the local Docker servers are throttled to avoid OOM. Idempotent so a partial run resumes.
acceptance_criteria: seed.py --only all --jobs N seeds multiple SCMs concurrently and prints a per-platform created/exists/skipped/failed summary.

title: Full end-to-end test orchestrator
description: scripts/full-test-run.sh chains unit tests, local env bring-up, seeding all 5 SCMs, a dry-analyze sweep asserting blob labels, the local wheel/time-bomb distribution test, amp analyze into the control repo, and /dryrun+/migrate into the dest org, with a per-phase pass/fail summary.
acceptance_criteria: Running the orchestrator executes each enabled phase and exits non-zero if any phase fails; phases are individually skippable.
notes: License-bypass path intentionally not tested
